output:
# PRD — In-app substitution approvals **Owner:** PM, Basketful · **Status:** Draft for review ## 1. Problem 11.8% of orders contain an out-of-stock item (1.7 per affected order, ≈0.2 per order overall). The shopper substitutes on judgement and the customer learns of the swap at the door, where **23% of substitutes are refused**: a wasted pick, a refund, a slower handover and a customer who feels unheard. Shoppers get no signal about what the customer would accept. ## 2. Goals and success metrics Goals: customers decide before checkout; shoppers don't slow down; nobody is overcharged; no licence breach. | Metric | Baseline | Target (90 days post-launch) | |---|---|---| | Substitutes refused at the door | 23% | ≤ 10% | | Substitution requests answered in-window | 74% (pilot, one store) | ≥ 75% network-wide | | Median shopper time, pick to checkout | 34 min | ≤ 35 min (guardrail) | | Customers charged above ordered price | not instrumented; assumed 0 | 0 | | Substitutions on restricted items | not instrumented | 0 | | Support contacts about substitutions | not instrumented — add pre-launch | −30% | ## 3. Non-goals - Reducing out-of-stock rates or fixing inventory data. - Free-text chat between shopper and customer. - Changing Terms §7.3 (escalated, §8). - Any substitution of alcohol, tobacco or pharmacy items. - Desktop web approval (mobile app, with SMS deep-link fallback). ## 4. Key decisions **Response window: 5 minutes, non-blocking.** Pilot: 38% respond within 1 min, 61% within 3, 74% within 5 — and 74% + 26% "never" = 100%, so **nobody responded between minute 5 and checkout**. Five minutes captures every response we would ever get; 60 seconds would time out 62% of requests. "Median under a minute" only holds among responders (38/74 ≈ 51%), not across requests. The shopper never waits: they flag the item, keep picking, and the app re-sequences the substitute to the end of the route. If the shopper reaches checkout with a request still open, it closes early and the default applies. **No-response default: the customer's order-level preference, with "Replace with the closest match" preselected.** Non-responders are unreachable during the order (no late responses in the pilot), so consent must be captured at checkout. Replace-by-default matches today's behaviour, keeps staples in the basket, and has no financial downside thanks to the price cap and door refusal. Refund-by-default would strip an item from ~26% of requests, including customers who simply missed the push. Preselection is A/B tested (§8). **Stakeholder requests** | Request | Decision | |---|---| | Ops (Stiles): 60-second timeout, auto-approve | Auto-approve as preselected default: **accepted**. 60 s: **rejected** — contradicted by the pilot curve. The "shoppers can't wait" concern is solved by a non-blocking window plus the 35-min guardrail, not by a short timer. | | Finance (Miles): charge the substitute's shelf price | **Rejected for v1** — breaches published §7.3 ("you will never pay more"). **Escalated** to Legal and Finance leadership for a Terms review. Mitigations now: rank same-or-lower-priced substitutes first; instrument upgrade cost per order so the v2 decision is data-backed. | | Compliance: restricted items refund-only | **Accepted** as a hard requirement (FR2). | ## 5. User stories **Customer** - See the original, the proposed substitute and the price I'll pay, and decide in one tap. - Pick a different replacement myself if I don't like the proposal. - Set "refund, don't replace" in advance for items I'm particular about. - Know exactly what happens if I miss the notification. **Shopper** - Propose a substitute in two taps and keep picking. - Get suggestions close in size and price so customers approve. - See a clear instruction before checkout: keep, remove or refund. - Be stopped from substituting anything my licence forbids. ## 6. Functional requirements 1. **Propose.** Marking an item OOS shows ranked suggestions (same category, matching size, same-or-lower price first); shopper may scan any other item. One request per OOS item, independent timers, grouped notifications. 2. **Restricted items.** Alcohol, tobacco, pharmacy: "Substitute" disabled, auto-refund, customer notified. Restricted items are also excluded as candidates for any original item (no new ID-check items enter an order). 3. **Notify.** Push with deep link; SMS deep link if push is undeliverable or disabled. 4. **Approval screen.** Original item; substitute (image, size, quantity); shelf price and **price you pay** = min(original, substitute) per unit; countdown; plain-language default statement; actions Approve / Choose another / Refund instead. WCAG AA: 44 px targets, aria-live countdown, no colour-only meaning. 5. **Timer.** 5:00 from proposal, server-authoritative; closes early when the shopper starts checkout. 6. **Default.** Applied at expiry from the order-level preference set at checkout (editable until the first request fires). 7. **Pricing.** Charge min(original, substitute) per unit; lower the pre-authorisation when cheaper; never raise it. 8. **Late responses.** Honoured until checkout starts; afterwards a rejection becomes a door-refusal instruction (no charge). 9. **Choose another.** Customer picks from the store's live-inventory list in the same category; shopper confirms on shelf; if unavailable, the request re-issues with the greater of remaining time and 2:00, unless the shopper is at checkout (default applies). 10. **Shopper view.** Per-item state (pending/approved/rejected/refunded), route re-sequencing, checkout prompts resolution of every open request. 11. **Audit and receipt.** Log proposal, decision, actor (customer/default), timestamps, price charged; receipt labels "approved by you" vs "replaced by default — refusable at the door". ## 7. Edge cases - Customer rejects after the substitute is already bagged → shopper removes it before checkout. - Substitute gone when shopper returns → new request if ≥ 2 min remain, else refund. - Pack mismatch (2 L vs 2×1 L) → cap the total at the original line price; show quantity explicitly. - Original on multibuy promo → cap at promo unit price; promo on remaining units preserved. - Customer edits or cancels the order mid-request → request voided. - Shopper reassigned → open requests transfer with timers intact. - Phone offline / notifications off → SMS; if nothing is delivered, the default still applies and the receipt flags it. - Weighed items → cap on per-kg price. - Customer taps a stale notification after checkout → "already checked out; refuse at the door for a refund". - Clock skew → countdown computed from server timestamps only. ## 8. Open questions 1. **Legal:** does §7.3 apply when the customer *chooses* a pricier alternative? Can Terms be revised with notice, and on what timeline? 2. **Finance:** quantify upgrade margin loss in v1 before any v2 pricing change. 3. **Generalisation:** the pilot is 1,200 requests at one store; run a two-week, three-store beta before locking the window. 4. **Default test:** should "Refund" be preselected for brand-sensitive categories (baby, allergen, dietary)? 5. **SMS fallback:** cost vs. uplift in response rate. 6. **Two options:** should shoppers be able to propose two substitutes at once? --- ## Prototype — customer approval screen ```html Basketful — Approve a replacement
Basketful

One item is out of stock

Order #48213 · Priya is still picking your order
Time left to respond 4:32

If you don't respond, we'll add this replacement — that's your order setting. You can still refuse it at the door for a full refund. Change setting

🥛
You ordered
Yeo Valley Organic Whole Milk
2 L · Qty 1 · £2.40
Out of stock
↓ Priya suggests
🥛
Replacement
Arla Organic Whole Milk
2 L · Qty 1 · Organic, same size
In stock
Shelf £2.65You pay £2.40
Price protected: you never pay more than the item you ordered. If a replacement is cheaper, you pay the cheaper price.

Your choice goes straight to Priya's handset.

``` ## Design rationale The screen answers three questions in reading order: how long do I have and what happens if I do nothing; what did I order versus what's proposed; what will I pay. The default lives inside the timer card as a plain sentence, not a footnote, because the 26% who never respond must understand the consequence — and that door refusal still exists. Price protection is explicit, with the shelf price struck through, so a pricier substitute never reads as an upsell. Three actions carry distinct weights: Approve is primary (it matches the default outcome and shows the price), Choose another is a bordered secondary, Refund is a full-width text button — visible and 44 px tall, not buried. Everything fits a 390×844 viewport without scrolling. The countdown is text plus a draining bar inside an aria-live region; the only JavaScript ticks the number, and the screen degrades gracefully without it.
